info.name: Modernizing Enterprise Applications — Behavior-Equivalence Suite
info.description: The behavior-equivalence suite (r02-plan S6, notification-plan S2, inventory-plan S2, payment-plan S2, build-plan.md §G/§D). Captured against the running Spring Boot monolith (examples/00-monolith). This collection is the project's equivalence gate: it is re-run UNCHANGED against each extracted service (starting with the Quarkus Review service, ch.15) and a service is only considered 'done' once it passes this same suite with no edits (build-plan.md §G load-bearing rule). Every request targets {{baseUrl}} so the identical collection can point at the monolith or at an extracted service's own port. Covers: (1) happy-path checkout — ADAPTED for the forthcoming ASYNC checkout contract (payment-plan.md S2, DRQ-047/DRQ-055): the POST is tolerant of `201` (today's synchronous monolith) or `202` (the future choreographed-saga payment service), and a BOUNDED-WAIT poll of GET /api/orders/{id} asserts the order strictly reaches the terminal `CONFIRMED` status — only the transport is relaxed, the terminal outcome and the stock-decrement side effect are unchanged and strict; (2) out-of-stock — left untouched/fully synchronous (inventory Reserve stays synchronous even after the payment extraction, so POST still returns `409` immediately); (3) payment-declined — ADAPTED the same way (DRQ-047/DRQ-055): POST tolerant of `402` (today's synchronous monolith — the whole checkout transaction is rolled back/compensated before the response, so there is no order to poll) or `202` (the saga — order persists PENDING, decline arrives later), then a BOUNDED-WAIT poll of GET /api/orders/{id} strictly asserting `PAYMENT_DECLINED` (saga path only) AND a BOUNDED-WAIT poll of GET /api/inventory/{sku} strictly asserting stock returns to net-zero (both paths) — the crux assertion (compensation via an in-line Release today, via the payment.declined choreography reaction later, DRQ-049) is never weakened; (4) the Review context contract (list, get-by-id, unauthenticated POST -> 401, authenticated POST -> 201, validation -> 400) — the first extraction's externally-observable surface — (5) the Notification context contract (DRQ-037): a checkout followed by a BOUNDED-WAIT poll of GET /api/notifications?customerId= so the identical assertion is correct whether the order-confirmation notification is written synchronously in-transaction (today's monolith, hits on the first attempt) or eventually via outbox -> Kafka -> consumer (the future async notification service, ch.17) — and (6) the Inventory Context Contract (inventory-plan.md S2, DRQ-046): the `/api/inventory` READ surface (list + get-by-sku + 404 for an unknown sku), asserted as a synchronous request/response (no bounded-wait — Reserve stays synchronous, DRQ-041) — distinct from, and NOT a duplicate of, the cross-seam inventory-mutation behavior already proven by Scenario 1 (stock decrements by ordered qty), Scenario 2 (out-of-stock -> 409, stock unchanged) and Scenario 3 (payment-declined -> stock rolled back, not left decremented), which remain the load-bearing inventory-equivalence checks the ch.19/ch.23 extractions must keep green across the seam.

item.name: 5a. Place order to trigger a confirmation notification -> 201 Created

exec: pm.test('Order status transitions straight to CONFIRMED', function () {
// Before-state for the poll below: the order/customer this checkout just
// created, plus a fresh retry budget — captured as collection variables so
// the folder is idempotent/re-runnable without a DB reset (mirrors the
// DRQ-037 bounded-wait eventual-consistency poll: only delay on a RETRY
// (attempts > 0), never on the first attempt. Against today's synchronous
// monolith the notification is already there on attempt 0, so this never
// sleeps and the folder passes immediately. Against the future async
// service (outbox -> Kafka -> SmallRye consumer) this gives each retry a
// short, bounded window for the event to be consumed. A plain busy-wait is
// used (not setTimeout) so the delay is honored identically by the Postman
// app and by newman's non-interactive sandbox before the request is sent.
while (Date.now() - start < delayMs) { /* intentional bounded busy-wait */ }
// Not observable yet and the retry budget is not exhausted: this is the
// ONLY branch that loops. Correct for BOTH backends — a synchronous
// backend matches on attempt 0 and never reaches here; an async backend
// keeps retrying (bounded) while outbox -> Kafka -> consumer catches up.
// Either found, or the bounded-wait budget is exhausted: assert the
// externally-observable contract (NotificationDto fields) — never raw DB
// rows — and stop retrying either way (goes RED here, not hung, when the
// notification never arrives — the DRQ-037 negative-check property).
pm.test('Order-confirmation notification for this checkout is observable within the bounded-wait budget (' + maxAttempts + ' x ' + delayMs + 'ms)', function () {
